alzheimer.name: Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP)
alzheimer.relevance: Central to amyloid plaque formation in Alzheimer disease
alzheimer.function: Involved in neuronal development and synaptic plasticity

alzheimer.name: Beta-Secretase 1 (BACE1)
alzheimer.function: Cleaves APP to produce amyloid-beta peptides
alzheimer.drugs: None approved; BACE1 inhibitors such as verubecestat and lanabecestat were discontinued after failed trials

alzheimer.name: Tau Protein (MAPT)
alzheimer.relevance: Forms neurofibrillary tangles characteristic of Alzheimer
alzheimer.function: Microtubule-associated protein involved in neuronal transport
alzheimer.drugs: None approved; anti-tau antibodies and aggregation inhibitors are in clinical trials

parkinson.name: Alpha-Synuclein
parkinson.relevance: Forms Lewy bodies in Parkinson disease
parkinson.function: Presynaptic protein involved in dopamine regulation
parkinson.drugs: None approved; anti-alpha-synuclein antibodies such as prasinezumab are in clinical trials

parkinson.name: LRRK2
parkinson.relevance: Most common genetic cause of Parkinson
parkinson.function: Kinase involved in autophagy and mitochondrial function
parkinson.drugs: None approved; LRRK2 kinase inhibitors such as BIIB122 are in clinical trials

parkinson.name: GBA (Glucocerebrosidase)
parkinson.drugs: None approved for Parkinson disease; the chaperone ambroxol is under investigation

diabetes.name: Insulin Receptor (INSR)
diabetes.relevance: Central to glucose metabolism and insulin signaling

diabetes.name: DPP-4 (Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4)
diabetes.relevance: Regulates incretin hormones that control blood glucose

diabetes.name: SGLT2 (Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2)
diabetes.function: Transports glucose from kidney filtrate back to blood

cancer.name: HER2 (Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2)
cancer.relevance: Amplified in approximately 20% of breast cancers

cancer.name: PD-1 (Programmed Cell Death Protein 1)
cancer.relevance: Immune checkpoint involved in cancer immune evasion
cancer.function: Inhibits T-cell activation allowing tumors to escape immunity

inflammation.name: TNF-alpha (Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha)
inflammation.function: Mediates systemic inflammation and immune responses

inflammation.name: IL-6 (Interleukin-6)
inflammation.function: Pro-inflammatory cytokine in acute phase response

inflammation.name: COX-2 (Cyclooxygenase-2)
inflammation.function: Enzyme converting arachidonic acid to prostaglandins

heart.name: ACE (Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme)
heart.relevance: Regulates blood pressure and cardiovascular function
heart.function: Converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II

heart.name: Beta-1 Adrenergic Receptor
heart.function: Mediates effects of epinephrine and norepinephrine on heart

hypertension.name: ACE (Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme)
hypertension.function: Converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II

hypertension.name: Angiotensin II Receptor Type 1
hypertension.relevance: Mediates vasoconstriction and blood pressure elevation
hypertension.function: G-protein coupled receptor for angiotensin II

teeth.name: Amelogenin X (AMELX)
teeth.function: Primary protein in developing tooth enamel
teeth.drugs: None approved; enamel and dentin regeneration approaches are experimental

teeth.name: Enamelin (ENAM)
teeth.drugs: None approved; enamel and dentin regeneration approaches are experimental

teeth.name: Dentin Sialophosphoprotein (DSPP)
teeth.drugs: None approved; enamel and dentin regeneration approaches are experimental

dental.name: Amelogenin X (AMELX)
dental.function: Primary protein in developing tooth enamel
dental.drugs: None approved; enamel and dentin regeneration approaches are experimental

bone.name: RANKL (Receptor Activator of NF-κB Ligand)
bone.relevance: Critical for bone remodeling and osteoclast formation

bone.name: Parathyroid Hormone Receptor
bone.relevance: Regulates calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism
bone.function: Mediates PTH effects on bone and kidney

asthma.name: IL-5 (Interleukin-5)
asthma.relevance: Promotes eosinophil survival in allergic asthma

arthritis.name: TNF-alpha (Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha)
arthritis.relevance: Major driver of rheumatoid arthritis inflammation

arthritis.name: IL-6 (Interleukin-6)
arthritis.relevance: Contributes to joint inflammation and destruction

pain.name: COX-2 (Cyclooxygenase-2)
pain.function: Produces prostaglandins involved in pain signaling

depression.name: Serotonin Transporter (SERT)
depression.relevance: Regulates serotonin levels in synaptic cleft

depression.name: Serotonin Receptor 5-HT2A
depression.drugs: Atypical antipsychotics used as adjuncts, such as Quetiapine; Psilocybin is under investigation

crohn.name: TNF-alpha (Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha)
crohn.relevance: Drives intestinal inflammation in Crohn disease

crohn.name: Integrin alpha-4 (ITGA4)
crohn.relevance: The alpha-4-beta-7 integrin directs lymphocytes into inflamed gut tissue
crohn.function: Subunit of integrins that mediate lymphocyte adhesion and migration

kidney.name: ACE (Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme)
kidney.relevance: Protects kidney function in chronic kidney disease
kidney.function: Regulates blood pressure and kidney filtration

kidney.name: SGLT2 (Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2)
kidney.relevance: Reduces kidney stress by lowering glucose reabsorption

sarcopenia.name: Myostatin (GDF8)
sarcopenia.relevance: Negative regulator of muscle growth, key target for sarcopenia
sarcopenia.function: Inhibits muscle cell growth and differentiation
sarcopenia.drugs: None approved for sarcopenia; myostatin pathway inhibitors have been studied in clinical trials

sarcopenia.name: IGF-1 (Insulin-like Growth Factor 1)
sarcopenia.relevance: Promotes muscle protein synthesis and prevents atrophy
sarcopenia.function: Stimulates growth and maintains muscle mass
sarcopenia.drugs: Mecasermin (approved only for severe primary IGF-1 deficiency)

sarcopenia.name: mTOR (Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin)
sarcopenia.relevance: Central regulator of muscle protein synthesis
sarcopenia.function: Controls cell growth and protein synthesis
sarcopenia.drugs: mTOR inhibitors Sirolimus and Everolimus are approved for other indications; none approved for sarcopenia

muscle.name: Myostatin (GDF8)
muscle.drugs: None approved for muscle wasting; myostatin pathway inhibitors have been studied in clinical trials

muscle.name: IGF-1 (Insulin-like Growth Factor 1)
muscle.drugs: Mecasermin (approved only for severe primary IGF-1 deficiency)

obesity.name: GLP-1 Receptor (GLP1R)
obesity.relevance: Regulates appetite and insulin secretion, and is a validated obesity target
obesity.function: G protein-coupled receptor for glucagon-like peptide 1

obesity.name: Melanocortin 4 Receptor (MC4R)
obesity.relevance: Central regulator of energy balance; variants cause monogenic obesity
obesity.function: Hypothalamic receptor that controls food intake and energy expenditure
obesity.drugs: Setmelanotide (approved for specific genetic forms of obesity)
